title: Bilal on the roof
hook: the once-enslaved Bilal climbs the Ka'ba to call the adhan

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Haqq: the statues fell as he recited, truth has come, and falsehood vanished away. Your line was truth has come.

Who gets the best seat at the celebration? At most victory parties it's the generals, the donors, the old families. On the day Mecca opened, the early biographies say, the Prophet ﷺ turned to one man and told him to climb onto the roof of the Ka'ba and call the prayer. Not a chief of Quraysh. Not one of his own relatives. Bilal: a Black man from Abyssinian stock, born enslaved, in this very city. Some of the Meccan nobles below watched him go up, and the reports say a few of them muttered about it. Then his voice went out over the valley.
screen: `WHO GETS THE BEST SEAT?` → `CLIMB UP AND CALL.` → `BILAL, BORN ENSLAVED.`

segments.voice: Go back to the early years in Mecca. Bilal was an early Muslim, and he belonged to a man named Umayya, one of the Prophet's fiercest enemies. The biographies say Umayya would drag him into the midday heat, lay him on the burning ground, and put a heavy rock on his chest, demanding he give up the one God. And Bilal would only say one word, over and over: ahad, ahad. One. One. Abu Bakr bought him and set him free. In Medina, Bilal's strong voice made him the first mu'adhdhin, the one who calls the adhan, five times a day. Now it's the conquest. The same streets, some of the same people. And the man they had crushed under a rock stands on the roof of the Ka'ba, calling: God is greatest. The Qur'an puts the principle in one line, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct." Not the richest, not the best born. Bilal on the roof made that verse visible. Muslims still honor him; mosques and children carry his name, and the muezzin's role is often traced back to him. This whole week has been one arc: a treaty that looked like losing, letters sealed and sent to kings, Safiyyah becoming a mother of believers, a head bowed on the camel, no blame on you today, truth has come. And at the top of it, Bilal.
screen: `AHAD, AHAD — ONE, ONE.` · `THE FIRST MU'ADHDHIN.` · `THE NOBLEST IS THE BEST IN CONDUCT.` · `THIS WEEK: A VICTORY WITHOUT REVENGE.` · then, large: `BILAL ON TOP.`

segments.voice: Think of someone around you who usually gets overlooked: the quiet one on the team, the person who cleans the building, the relative who never gets asked for an opinion. Picture them in the place of honor, and ask yourself what small thing would put them there: asking their advice, saying their name with thanks, giving them the good seat. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.
Bilal, the once-enslaved caller of the prayer, lifted to the top of the Ka'ba on the day Mecca opened.
Your line: bilal on top. From under the rock to the roof. That's the week.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Bilal as the first muezzin, and the adhan he called is still sung from mosques five times a day; his story is often told to teach that nobility lies in conduct, not birth.

original.note: Arabic: the one who calls the adhan, the call to prayer. Bilal was the first.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man with a good voice got a job.
what it means: the tortured, once-enslaved Bilal lifted above the nobles, the verse about nobility made visible.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Ishaq places Bilal's adhan on the Ka'ba on the day of the conquest; 49:13 grounds rank in conduct, not lineage.
